subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw repair existing same-parent compaction retry forks by deleting dead-end compaction entries during session-file repair, or limit the fix to future write-side prevention and leave existing corrupted files to doctor/manual recovery?
rationale: The issue is a real session-state bug, but repairing already-persisted files changes stored session data and needs maintainer-owned policy rather than an automatic cleanup decision.

options.title: Accept narrow load-time repair
options.body: Refresh the linked PR so only dead-end same-parent compaction siblings are removed, including incremental-cache coverage and upgrade proof.

options.title: Prevent future forks only
options.body: Fix the compaction retry writer to be idempotent or supersede the first attempt, but leave existing corrupted transcripts untouched.

options.title: Move cleanup to doctor
options.body: Keep runtime repair non-deleting and add an explicit operator-triggered doctor repair for affected historical JSONL files.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow load-time repair
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR so only dead-end same-parent compaction siblings are removed, including incremental-cache coverage and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of the validated transcript repair cache makes this the best available routing target for the unresolved integration decision.
